A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PoLAR research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: V1 reports original fine-tuning experiments, matrix-factorization simulations, stable-rank analyses, and runtime measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds a GaLore comparison on commonsense reasoning tasks.

M1.justification: The polar parameterization, orthogonality constraints, unconstrained scale matrix, initialization, and landing-field optimization remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–3 retain the same procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same commonsense datasets, GLUE tasks, MetaMathQA training, GSM8K/MATH evaluation, and matrix-factorization scenarios. The added GaLore comparison uses existing task coverage.

E2.justification: GaLore, previously only cited, is evaluated against PoLAR in v2 Appendix F.4 and Table 8 using rank-16 Llama-2-7B. Existing LoRA, DoRA, and other comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: The new GaLore experiment adopts the existing commonsense setup and specifies scale 2, projection refreshes at 15% training increments, and learning rates of 1e-5 and 4e-5. Settings for retained experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: The parameterization/gradient ablation in Table 1, stable-rank analyses, feasibility checks, runtime comparisons, and Gemma-3-12B learning-rate study are retained. The added GaLore benchmark comparison introduces no separate ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report four GLUE seeds with standard deviations, single-seed large-model experiments, and the same median/IQR runtime measurement procedure. The GaLore results introduce no new uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 Table 8 adds GaLore accuracies with averages of 69.10 and 73.57 at its two learning rates, alongside PoLAR's retained 74.00 result. Existing numerical results and plotted findings remain unchanged, including v1 Table 8 becoming v2 Table 9.

T1.justification: The convergence theorems, assumptions, lemmas, and proofs in Appendices C–E are retained. Definition 1 moves from v1 Appendix C.1 to v2 Section 2.1 and restates the same polar decomposition using the method's notation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the claims about directional-diversity collapse, PoLAR's parameterization, faster canonical convergence, and gains across the same three task groups. The added comparison does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V2 qualifies the introductory expressiveness discussion with rank assumptions depending on pretrained and target models. Its condensed future-work paragraph drops v1 Appendix A's hypotheses connecting rank collapse to over-regularization and altered incremental learning. Stated empirical limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds GaLore configuration details in Appendix F.4 but removes the explicit experimental-code repository link from Section 4. Existing implementation and hardware details are retained; the removed link does not establish that the repository became unavailable.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 expands discussion to concurrent StelLA, LoRA-XS initialization, and subspace optimizers. V2 removes one regularization citation and Appendix B's discussion of invariant LoRA optimization. Stable-rank related work is relocated rather than removed.

P1.justification: V2 brings the polar-decomposition explanation into Section 2.1, moves stable-rank background to Appendix B, and condenses future directions into the conclusion. Related-work prose, affiliations, and acknowledgements change, while most of the narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds the GaLore table and adopts NeurIPS styling, including revised title formatting, headings, and removal of running headers. Existing displays are retained with some resizing, relocation, and caption edits; their visual content is largely unchanged.

improvement.justification: The documented GaLore comparison and expanded discussion of concurrent and subspace methods modestly strengthen comparative support and positioning. Bringing the existing polar definition into Section 2.1 improves accessibility. These limited gains are partly offset by removal of the experimental-code link; the method, theory, and previous results remain unchanged.
